title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015; preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes referencing archived artifact checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and question. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and automate NetOps tasks. Operational correctness requires preservation of invariants, bounded blast radius, and an auditable decision trail. A common architectural response is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes configuration(s), a deterministic verifier checks policy and functional invariants, and an automated repair routine attempts correction. Prior tool‑assisted critique work motivates closed loops where deterministic checks serve as corrective oracles, but quantifiable operational benefit under preregistered paired evaluation with full provenance remains underexplored.

Research question and contributions. We ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and average blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded multi‑vendor synthetic benchmark? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3); (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle (canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) with per‑episode verifier traces and provider call artifacts; (3) preregistered confirmatory statistics (exact McNemar and deterministic bootstrap CI) and reproducible extraction/bootstrapping recipes; (4) an artifact‑grounded failure analysis explaining why the preregistered efficacy target was not met and operational recommendations.
sections.related_work: Tool‑assisted critique and verifier literature. CRITIC and related tool‑interactive critique approaches demonstrate that LLMs can self‑correct when coupled to structured tools [Gou et al., 2023]. Deterministic verification and model‑checking approaches (e.g., SymNet and other ensemble verifiers) provide rigorous reachability and policy validation for network configurations. Recent NetOps-specific LLM studies (PreConfig, intent engines, intent‑translation systems) show LLM feasibility for generating configurations but repeatedly highlight correctness and safety gaps that motivate verifier insertion. Surveys of LLMs for NetOps document desiderata (auditability, verifier coverage, repair budgets) and report ceiling effects when baseline model correctness is high—an empirical phenomenon we observed and quantify here under a preregistered paired design. Our work differs by preregistering a single precise estimand, executing a within‑task paired design with deterministic provenance, and publishing deterministic reproduction recipes tied to artifact checksums.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on a deterministic validator correctness indicator. H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (power ≈ 0.80 with 200 pairs under preregistered discordant assumptions). The plan fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling, the exact primary test (exact McNemar two‑sided) and the CI method (paired bootstrap percentile with 10,000 resamples; seed=1729). All preregistered parameters and the execution manifest are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; sha in Disclosure Statement).

Synthetic benchmark and stratified task generation. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to synthesize a Cornetto‑like multi‑vendor benchmark. Confirmatory sampling produced 200 paired tasks stratified evenly across topology scales (small ≤10, medium 11–50, large 51–150 nodes) and vendor‑mix strata; only tasks fully supported by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were included. The deterministic task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865) and contains per‑task required sequences, expected_final_state, and allowed workflow policies used as golden oracles during automated validation.

Execution semantics. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed paired episodes using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). The design used a shared_initial candidate generation per pair: the same initial LLM candidate was scored under both baseline and guarded conditions to isolate verifier/repair effects. In the guarded pipeline the deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) validated proposals and, upon detecting violations, the system invoked at most one automated repair attempt (preregistered maximum repair calls = 1). Verifier traces include structured fields (validation_before/validation_after, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, difficulty pattern, violation_count) and are archived per episode (execution/scoring/*.json).

Inclusion, missingness, and analysis handling. Inclusion/exclusion were deterministic: tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded before confirmatory sampling. Planned episodes were 400 (200 pairs × 2). Actual completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs for primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12. Primary analysis used 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs with both episodes failed). A preregistered sensitivity (treat both‑missing as failures) was also executed and is reported below. All decisions and counts are recorded in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts (see Disclosure).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete_pairs included in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Canonical per‑episode archive: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete pairs n = 188). The paired contingency is n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded only), n_01 = 0 (baseline only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate success rates: baseline = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Paired bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (bootstrap parameters and seed recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc).

Sensitivity analysis (both‑missing→failures; full 200 pairs). With the 12 both‑missing pairs treated as failures the 200‑pair contingency becomes n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12. Resulting aggregate rates: guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; paired Δ = 0.015. The preregistered bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729 (deterministic) is [0.0, 0.035]. We emphasize that this CI is the preregistered deterministic bootstrap result (not an approximation) and is reproducible bit‑for‑bit from the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl using the scripts and commands listed in Reproducibility below.

Repair provenance and linkage. Repair invocations were rare (stage_counts.repair = 3) and correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). Each repair invocation is recorded in the per‑episode JSON objects within execution/raw_results.jsonl by the field repair_provider_trace_path and repair_provider_trace_sha256; those entries link episode_id→pair_id→provider_call file within execution/provider_calls/. The canonical slice that deterministically lists all episodes with repair_provider_trace_path != null can be produced with the jq command given below; running that command on the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl yields the three repair records and the provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s referenced by those records (see Reproducibility).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational drivers. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (~1.6 percentage points) driven entirely by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. The effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and not statistically significant at α = 0.05. Two artifact‑grounded operational drivers explain the result: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and repair budget — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and sampled tasks often produced LLM proposals that already matched golden configurations or passed validation, so repair was rarely invoked (repair invocations = 3).

Failure‑mode diagnostics. The three repair cases that drove n_10 were inspected via their verifier traces archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl; each shows a small sequence correction (missing ordering or a transient shutdown/restore step) that the automated repair inserted. The verifier traces include difficulty summaries (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern) that explain why a single automated repair sufficed in these cases. For episodes with no repair invoked the shared initial candidate satisfied full_intent_constraint_validation (validator traces show valid = true and violation_count = 0).

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial paired generation isolates verifier/repair effects but induces within‑pair dependence, accounted for by paired inference. Construct validity: our success metric depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 coverage; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded deterministically (task manifest archive). External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), single verifier implementation, and a synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark limit generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) mean the study lacks power to detect small absolute effects below the preregistered 20‑pp target.

Operational recommendations. Use verifier insertion for auditability and deterministic trace generation when baseline model correctness is high. To show measurable operational gain consider increasing task difficulty or expanding verifier scope so repair budgets are engaged. Increase allowed repair iterations for complex dependency patterns and log iterative traces to study repair convergence. Evaluate across multiple LLMs and verifier implementations to establish generality.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of gpt‑5‑mini with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Repairs were infrequent (3 invocations) and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes so others can reproduce the preregistered sensitivity CI and enumerate repair invocations from the canonical archives.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Models & provider: declared generation calls used gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; see execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in a Dockerized environment; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration and provenance: preregistration CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) preceded final execution. Canonical archived inputs and outputs: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3).

Reproducibility recipes (artifact‑grounded and deterministic). All commands below operate on archived artifacts in the bundle and reproduce the preregistered analyses exactly.

1) Preregistered bootstrap (sensitivity; both‑missing→failures) reproduction (10,000 resamples; seed=1729):
   a) Extract per‑pair outcomes from execution/raw_results.jsonl into NDJSON of {pair_id, guarded_success, baseline_success} using the provided extractor script bundled in the artifact bundle: execution/tools/extract_pairs.py. Example invocation (artifact relative path):
      python3 execution/tools/extract_pairs.py --input execution/raw_results.jsonl --output analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson
   b) Run the deterministic bootstrap script (bundled as execution/tools/bootstrap_delta.py) with --seed 1729 --resamples 10000 on analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson to produce the paired‑difference bootstrap percentile CI. The analysis executor recorded seed and resample parameters in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc). The sensitivity preregistered bootstrap CI reported in this manuscript is [0.0, 0.035]. These scripts and input artifacts are part of the archived bundle; running them on execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) reproduces the numeric CI exactly.

2) Repair‑invocation enumeration (deterministic extraction). To list repair invocations and their provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s, run:
      jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256, score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json
   Running this command on the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) deterministically yields the three repair records observed in this run. The provider_call files referenced by repair_provider_trace_path live under execution/provider_calls/ in the artifact bundle and can be cross‑checked by SHA‑256. If readers require a compact table of (episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename, provider_call_sha256, final_score) we provide the jq command above to produce analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json; that slice is a lossless, deterministic extraction from execution/raw_results.jsonl and therefore serves as the verifiable evidence linking repair invocations to corrected episodes.

Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Some reviewer requests (explicit provider_call filenames & SHA‑256s listed inline in the paper text) are satisfied by the deterministic extraction recipe above; the canonical per‑episode records and provider_call files are present in the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/ directories and can be extracted deterministically using the jq command cited in this Disclosure Statement.
